A caregiving companion

Nori

Clarity and calm for the people who carry the care.

When someone you love is unwell, the hardest part isn't the loving — it's the not knowing. Nori stands beside you, so care feels less like a maze and more like a path.

01 — The weight of caring

Caring for someone shouldn't mean carrying it alone.

Behind every patient is someone keeping track — of the medicines, the appointments, the bills, the questions no one had time to answer. The love is never the problem. The overwhelm is.

A

Scattered information

Records live across portals, paperwork, and half-remembered conversations. Nothing sits in one place.

B

Caregiver overwhelm

Coordinator, advocate, scheduler, note-taker — a dozen roles at once, and no handbook for any of them.

C

Patients feeling unseen

Waiting for a ride, for an answer, for someone to notice — a quiet isolation no one intended.

D

Anxious transitions

The uncertain gaps between hospital, home, and the next appointment — where worry lives.

02 — What Nori is

A companion for the care journey — not another system to manage.

Nori isn't a chart or a portal. It's a calmer way to move through care — gathering the scattered pieces into one clear picture, and standing beside families in the moments that feel heaviest.

One clear picture. Everything about a person's care, brought together — so nothing important slips through.

Language you can act on. Confusion turned into plain, human words — the kind that help you decide what to do next.

Steady, together. A family holding the same understanding — sharing the load instead of the worry.

A calmer place to stand — right in your hand.

04 — What it feels like

Three quiet promises.

01

Stay informed

Everything about their care, gathered into one clear place — so you always know where things stand, without hunting for it.

02

Stay connected

Family and the people helping, all on the same page — sharing what needs doing, instead of each carrying the worry alone.

03

Stay supported

A steady presence for the hard moments — answers when you need them, and calm for the times you don't have the words.

05 — Why Nori exists

It began with a question we couldn't answer.

A couple of months ago, I lost my uncle. In the weeks that followed, what stayed with me most wasn't only the grief — it was watching the people who had cared for him turn the same thought over and over.

"What else could I have done?"

That regret, I came to understand, wasn't a failure of love. It was a failure of clarity — they had given everything they had, inside a system that rarely made it easy to know whether it was enough.

It took me back to the year before, when I'd spent time observing clinical trials. I kept returning to what I'd seen in those rooms — patients waiting for a ride, for an answer, for someone to notice them. People who felt like a case number in the middle of their own care.

Somewhere between those two experiences — my family's regret and those quiet clinical rooms — I began thinking about how I could help. Nori is what took shape: a way for patients to feel seen and supported, for families to act with clarity and confidence, and for fewer people to be left asking the question mine couldn't put down.

Nori is built for families navigating care together.

No noise, no pressure. Just a calmer place to stand when someone you love needs you.
